claims.text: Systematic variation of alloying elements can establish property-composition relationships in high-entropy alloys.
Property-composition relationships can improve the accuracy of determining melting temperatures in high-entropy alloys.
Property-composition relationships can improve the accuracy of determining enthalpies of fusion in high-entropy alloys.
Property-composition relationships can improve the accuracy of determining entropies of fusion in high-entropy alloys.
Property-composition relationships can improve the accuracy of determining volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
Property-composition relationships can improve the accuracy of determining liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed property-composition approach can determine thermodynamic properties more efficiently than current methods.
Current experimental methods and theoretical models have limited applicability across high-entropy alloys.
Current experimental methods and theoretical models have limited accuracy for high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
The proposed approach is applicable across the high-entropy-alloy family over varying compositions and at high temperatures.
Quantitative performance and applicability depend on the specific alloying elements and compositions.
